rounds.text: The strongest case against Nisus Services Co Ltd centres on severe fundamental deterioration and a wholesale flight of institutional capital. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by -37% [E16], accompanied by a net profit drop of -42% YoY [E58] and accelerating earnings deceleration [E60]. Operating margins have experienced dramatic compression, falling -11 percentage points over three years to 33% in March 2026 [E24], and plunging -43 percentage points in the March 2026 quarter compared to the year-ago period [E25]. Compounding these operational headwinds, the stock sits at just 16% of its 52-week range [E5] and has suffered a -47% price decline over the past year [E20]. This operational weakness is compounded by troubling quality-of-earnings signals and governance risks. Reported earnings are tainted by Rs 22.8 Cr of other income [E51], alongside a suspiciously low tax rate [E49] and worsening debtor days stretching from 77.5 to 102 days [E52]. Institutional investors have aggressively exited the stock, with foreign holdings dropping from 3.22% to 0.14% and domestic institutions falling from 5.80% to 2.55% [E36, E37], culminating in negative institutional money flow [E38] and 32.0% of promoter holdings being pledged [E50]. Furthermore, the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E48]. A severe top-line contraction casts serious doubt on the sustainability of current operations, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of -37% [E16], alongside year-over-year sales drops of -38% [E59] and net profit drops of -42% [E58]. Furthermore, reported earnings quality is heavily compromised by a massive 22.8 crore block of other income [E51], while debtor days have bloated from 77.5 to 102 days [E52], and institutional confidence has sharply eroded through heavy foreign and domestic divestment alongside negative money flow signals [E36, E37, E38]. Alarmingly, promoters have pledged 32.0% of their holding [E50] and the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Conceded: the company boasts a robust 5-year compounded profit growth of 85% [E17] and a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x [E32].
